lessons.title: What Lives Under the Sea?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least four sea creatures.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of sea creatures.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and name sea creatures found in the ocean, sorting by size or type.
key_questions: What sea creatures do you know?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sea creature vocabulary — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look at pictures of sea creatures together.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Rainbow Fish' by Marcus Pfister
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the fish's feelings changed.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing how the Rainbow Fish learned about sharing and friendship.
key_questions: Why was the fish lonely at first?
What did he learn about sharing?

differentiation.extension: Explain the story's message in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and understanding of a moral message — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Discuss the importance of sharing and kindness.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you shared something with a friend.

lessons.title: Counting Fish
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count fish counters accurately up to 10+.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a group of fish pictures together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort fish counters into groups, recording totals.
key_questions: Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.

lessons.title: Making a Sparkly Rainbow Fish Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a fish craft and add a sparkly scale using materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the Rainbow Fish's special sparkly scale.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a fish craft with colourful scales, adding one sparkly/foil scale, linking to the story's sharing theme.
resources_needed: Fish template, coloured paper, foil paper

differentiation.extension: Cut own scale shapes and arrange in a pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and pattern-making — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display fish crafts together as an 'under the sea' display.
lessons.home_link: Make a fish craft together at home.

lessons.title: How Do Fish Breathe Underwater?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say simply that fish use gills to breathe underwater.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we breathe using our lungs.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce simply that fish use gills to take oxygen from water, comparing to how humans breathe.
key_questions: How is that different from how we breathe?

differentiation.extension: Explain the comparison in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of animal adaptation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up how fish breathe together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Consolidation - Reading Sea Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple sea-themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading sea-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the fish has a fin').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading sea words over the week.

lessons.title: Sorting Sea Creatures by Size
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order sea creatures by size.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a size comparison of sea creatures (whale vs seahorse).
lessons.main_activity: Children order sea creature picture cutouts from smallest to biggest, using comparative language.
resources_needed: Sea creature picture cutouts of varying sizes
lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of sea creature size order.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of toys or objects at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Sea Creatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different sea creatures.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a jellyfish floats vs a shark darts.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating jellyfish floating, sharks darting, and octopuses wiggling their tentacles.
resources_needed: Open space, optional blue fabric for 'waves'
key_questions: Can you dart like a shark?

differentiation.extension: Invent an original sea creature movement

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite sea creature movement performed.
lessons.home_link: Act out a sea creature movement for family.

lessons.title: Coral Reefs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a coral reef is.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of colourful coral reefs.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss coral reefs as a colourful underwater habitat for many sea creatures, and why they need to be protected.
key_questions: What do you notice about the coral reef?
Why is it important to protect it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note environmental awareness — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what a coral reef is.
lessons.home_link: Look up coral reef pictures together.

lessons.title: Writing Sea Creature Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label for a sea creature.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw a sea creature and attempt to write its name using known phonics sounds.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled sea creature pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw and label a sea creature together at home.

lessons.title: Counting Octopus Legs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in a repeated group (8 legs per octopus).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting spider legs from Week 27.
lessons.main_activity: Children count octopus legs (8 per octopus) using counters, and count multiple octopuses' legs together.
key_questions: How many legs does one octopus have?
How many legs do two octopuses have altogether?

differentiation.extension: Count legs of 2-3 octopuses and add totals

lessons.assessment_notes: Note counting in groups understanding — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of octopus leg counting.
lessons.home_link: Count legs on toy sea creatures at home.

lessons.title: Ocean Pollution and Caring for the Sea
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way to help look after the ocean.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the environmental care theme from Week 17 (Arctic).
lessons.main_activity: Very simply discuss that plastic pollution can harm sea creatures, and think of ways to help (recycling, not littering).
resources_needed: Simple ocean pollution awareness picture cards
key_questions: How can we help look after the ocean?

differentiation.extension: Suggest a way to help the ocean

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early environmental awareness — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class list of ways to help look after the ocean.
lessons.home_link: Do one thing to help look after the environment at home (recycle, pick up litter).

lessons.title: Retelling 'The Rainbow Fish'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and fish props.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Under the Sea Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 using a sea-themed activity.
lessons.main_activity: Using fish counters split between two 'fish bowls', children practise and record all number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Under the Sea Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the ocean and sea creatures learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Under the Sea' display summarising sea creatures, coral reefs, and caring for the ocean.
key_questions: What have we learned about the sea?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the sea with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: Sea-Themed Reading Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read sea-themed sentences fluently.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading a range of sea-themed sentences with increasing fluency.
key_questions: Can you read it more quickly?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reading fluency progress — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading sea sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sorting, Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sorting, and number bond skills learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting fish/octopus legs, sorting sea creatures by size, number bonds to 10.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and sorting over the weekend.

lessons.title: Under the Sea Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement and craft in a class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining sea creature movements from Tuesday, with fish crafts displayed.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the under the sea week.
lessons.home_link: Perform a sea creature movement for family this weekend.
